ai.description: This gecko reaches 8 cm SVL. It is reddish-brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a pale underside. Key features include strongly curved toes and a granular, non-tuberculate dorsal skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus rubidus* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, reddish-brown dorsal blotches and the absence of a precloacal groove, unlike most other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus rubidus* inhabits the tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, frequently found on tree trunks and rocky surfaces at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Andaman bent-toed gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates on tree trunks and rocky surfaces within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus rubidus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, primarily from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus rubidus* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring across various elevations throughout this Indian archipelago.
